title: A multi-region CloudTrail trail is enabled and logging management events
description: Without an active multi-region trail, API activity in some regions is not recorded, leaving no audit trail for incident response.

title: MFA is enabled for the root user
description: The root user has unrestricted access to the account. Without MFA, a leaked password gives full account takeover.
expected_state: Root user has an MFA device registered
remediation: 1. Sign in as the root user and open Security credentials. | 2. Under Multi-factor authentication (MFA), choose Assign MFA device and complete enrolment (prefer a hardware/FIDO2 key). | 3. Store the root credentials and recovery material offline; use the root user only for tasks that require it.

title: No access keys exist for the root user
description: Root access keys are long-lived credentials with unrestricted privileges and cannot be scoped down.
expected_state: No root access keys
remediation: 1. Sign in as the root user, open Security credentials > Access keys. | 2. Make each root access key inactive, confirm nothing breaks, then delete it. | 3. Use IAM roles / IAM Identity Center for programmatic access instead.

title: Root user does not use a virtual MFA device
description: CIS recommends a hardware MFA device for root. The API exposes virtual MFA devices by serial number but cannot distinguish a hardware token from a FIDO2/passkey, so PASS means 'MFA present and not virtual'.
current_state: Root MFA is not enabled at all
expected_state: Root MFA is a hardware / FIDO2 device (not a virtual authenticator app)
remediation: 1. Sign in as root > Security credentials > MFA. | 2. Remove the virtual MFA device and register a hardware TOTP token or FIDO2 security key.

title: MFA is enabled for all IAM users with a console password
description: Console users without MFA are exposed to password phishing, reuse and brute force.
current_state: Console password set but no MFA
expected_state: Every IAM user with a console password has MFA active
remediation: 1. IAM > Users > select the user > Security credentials > Assign MFA device. | 2. Better: remove IAM console users and federate through IAM Identity Center with enforced MFA.

title: Active access keys are rotated within 90 days

remediation: 1. Create a second key for the user, update the application to use it, and verify. | 2. Deactivate then delete the old key. | 3. Prefer IAM roles with temporary credentials so no long-lived key exists.
